## Lab 07 Assignment - Group 20

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)  # devtools::install_github("tidymodels/broom")
library(cowplot)
```

```{r}
biopsy <- read_csv("https://wilkelab.org/classes/SDS348/data_sets/biopsy.csv")
```

```{r}
pca_fit <- biopsy %>% 
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>% # retain only numeric columns
  prcomp(scale = TRUE) # do PCA on scaled data

pca_fit
```

```{r}
pca_fit <- biopsy %>% 
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>% # retain only numeric columns
  scale() %>% # scale data
  prcomp() # do PCA

pca_fit
```

### Ridge Density Plots of all features

```{r}
library(ggridges)
```

```{r}
biopsy |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = -outcome, names_to = "feature", values_to = "value") |> 
  
  ggplot(aes(x = value,
             y = feature,
             fill = outcome)) +
  
  geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) +
  
  theme_ridges() + 
  
  labs(title = "Ridge Density Plots of all features",
       subtitle = "Divided by tumor expression outcome",
       x = "Values (0-10)",
       y = "Feature",
       fill = "Outcome")
```

**Analysis:** It's possible to see that malignant and benign cells are very different.

Some features can even be used as strong predictors of malignancy, like *uniform_cell_size, bare_nuclei,* and *uniform_cell_shape,* as these features exhibit sharp differences between the two possible outcomes.
